description: The qemu-image-build GitHub Actions workflow downloads yq from a mutable GitHub release URL with no SHA-256 verification, chmods it executable, and runs it. The same job subsequently calls aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials to assume secrets.CONTROL_PLANE_PROD_ROLE via OIDC. Because GitHub release assets can be replaced in-place, a compromised mikefarah/yq maintainer could swap the v4.45.1 arm64 asset for a trojan that waits for the AWS credentials to be configured and exfiltrates them. Those STS credentials grant whatever the prod control-plane role can do (publish AMIs, write artifact buckets), cascading into downstream customer impact.
reproduction: Compromise a mikefarah/yq maintainer token or gain repo write access
Re-upload the v4.45.1 yq_linux_arm64 asset with a trojan that forks a background process polling for AWS_* env vars / ~/.aws/credentials and POSTs them out
Wait for the next push to supabase/postgres to trigger the qemu-image-build workflow
Trojan runs, waits for configure-aws-credentials to assume CONTROL_PLANE_PROD_ROLE, exfiltrates the STS credentials
Use the stolen credentials to push a backdoored AMI that is rolled out to customers
technical_details: `curl -L .../mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.45.1/yq_linux_arm64 -o yq && chmod +x yq` fetches a release asset that the upstream repo can silently replace without changing the tag, and no checksum is verified before execution. The downloaded binary runs with the job's filesystem and environment, so it can read ~/.aws, AWS_* env vars, or the metadata hop once configure-aws-credentials populates them.
title: CI downloads unverified binary then assumes production AWS role
